one_month_reasoning: No Intel earnings in the window (next print late January 2027). Scheduled read-throughs: Micron's fiscal Q1 results in mid-December (memory pricing; TrendForce sees PC DRAM +13-18% q/q in 4Q26 [16], a headwind for PC units) and December PC sell-through data. Unscheduled: a 14A customer announcement (Tan: next two quarters [18]) is upside skew; the securities suit filed Nov 13 [26] and further substrate news are downside. After a ~60% fall from the September high [31] there is no clear momentum or reversal edge, so the ladder is a symmetric lognormal around $59.66 at monthly vol 0.86/3.5 = 24.6%.

fair_value.method: Quarterly driver build (PC units x Intel revenue per unit; supply-bound DCAI; segment margins; Foundry/corporate loss) gives FY2028 revenue ~$72.4B and NTM EPS ~$1.55 at the horizon. P/E 37.7x (peer median 22.4x shrunk toward own 42.9x, k 0.8) = $61.96 (w 0.65); SOTP (Products 15x EV/EBIT on $20.7B, Foundry loss x6, net debt and NCI) = $46.69 (w 0.35); both include a 30% x $60B 14A option. Engine base $56.62.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at horizon ~$1.55 (build: EBIT ~10.6B, net interest ~0, 12% tax, NCI ~0.96B, 5,369M shares) x 37.7x + 14A option $3.3

inputs_detail.derivation: Company non-GAAP Q4 2026 rate 11% [1]; Q3 2026 GAAP 11.6% (F113). GAAP FY2025 98.3% (F111) was valuation-allowance driven (F115), a one-off. 12% = the stated 11% plus one point for lower R&D credit share as profits rise.

Q3 2026 diluted 5,307M (F33), 5,315M outstanding Oct 23 (F85). +1.0%: FY2023-FY2024 diluted grew 4,212 -> 4,280 (+1.6%, F28, F29) with no equity raise; SBC ~2.4B a year at ~$60 = ~40M shares (0.75%); no buybacks, dividend suspended (F57).
Peer median NTM P/E 22.4x (AMD 39.3, QCOM 22.4, NVDA 14.5, AVGO 18.7, MRVL 37.2 [27]). Own NTM P/E on the build: price 59.66 / FY2027 EPS ~1.39 = 42.9x. Exit = 22.4 x (42.9/22.4)^0.8 = 37.7x.

Tan: 14A customers could be ready to announce over the next two quarters [18]; BofA (Arya) downgraded on little evidence of major external foundry customers [24]. 30% probability; $60B ~ 18% of today's ~$317B market cap (59.66 x 5,315M, F85) as the value a credible TSMC second source adds.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Products 20,700 x 15 = 310.5B; Foundry/other -10,105 x 6 = -60.6B; net debt at H 0.6B; NCI 16.6B; +14A option 18B; / 5,369M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Debt 50,134 - cash 21,846 - short-term investments 32,159 = -3,871 (F87). NCI on the balance sheet 16,642 at Sep 26 2026 [1].

QCOM (closest mature client-SoC peer) trades 22.4x NTM P/E and 15.1x trailing EV/EBITDA [27]; Intel Products are losing server share to Arm and AMD [17,19], so 15x EV/EBIT (~17x P/E at 12% tax) sits below the peer median.
Losses narrowing (Foundry -3,168 Q2 2025 -> -1,853 Q3 2026 [1,2]; 18A cost -40% [18]); capitalising the loss at 6x assumes it fades over ~6 years.

downside.story: P10: PC units fall a further ~6 pts a year below base (memory shortage and OEM destock run through 2027 [16]), client price/mix gives back the 2026 step (-5 pts), DCAI output 15% lower (substrate shortage and Fab 28 aftermath persist; Arm reaches 30%+ of server CPUs [17]), segment margins 4-6 pts lower, Foundry losses 12% wider with no 14A anchor, and the P/E falls 10 turns toward the peer median.

base.story: Median: PC units fall ~25% y/y in Q4 2026 and ~6% in 2027 before a small 2028 recovery; client revenue per unit gives back part of its 2026 step; DCAI grows ~29% in 2027 as supply unlocks, then ~9%; Foundry losses narrow slowly; market keeps a trough-cycle P/E (37.7x) on ~$1.55 NTM EPS.

upside.story: P90: PC units recover faster (Counterpoint flat 2027 [15] plus a 2028 refresh), Xeon supply unlocks (+12% DCAI) while shortage pricing holds, margins +3-4 pts, Foundry losses narrow 15% and a named 14A customer lifts the multiple 8 turns.

reasoning: Industry lane. The September-November collapse ($123 to ~$52-60 [31]) came from the PC side of the chain: Gartner -22.4%, IDC -20.1%, Omdia -21%, Counterpoint -21% Q3 units [6,13,14,15], Q4 forecasts -24% to -27% [14,15], OEM finished-goods inventories building into 1Q27 [16], plus Intel's own supply problems (Fab 28 explosion ~$600M revenue [21], substrate shortage [22]) that capped the one strong segment. Server demand is the offset: TrendForce sees server CPU units +40% in 2027 but Arm reaching ~30% share [17], AMD Data Center +97% y/y [20] and Mercury showing AMD server share still rising [19], so Intel's DCAI growth is supply- and share-limited. I built CCPG from industry units x Intel revenue per unit (which jumped +19-22% y/y in Q2-Q3 2026 on pricing and pull-ins, so I let it fade), DCAI from supply, and kept Foundry losses narrowing slowly. Guidance: the 2026 beats came from channel pull-ins, so I did not apply the record to Q4. Base case $56.62 (-5%) with a fat left tail ($26.33 P10) and $99.12 P90, consistent with 86% realized vol. Research was limited: WebFetch budget ran out (shared across agents), so post-print consensus, 2024 CCG comparatives and earlier guides could not be re-opened (gap_note).

drivers.label: DCAI revenue (supply-bound Xeon output)
drivers.source: Intel releases [1,2,3,4]; TIKR CFO remarks [22]; Fab 28 [21]; TrendForce server CPU [17]; Futurum [18]; AMD [20]
drivers.derivation: Actuals from releases [1-4]. DCAI is supply-bound (CEO: unlock supply to meet extraordinary Xeon demand [18]); revenue = shippable output. Q4 2026 8,200 = Q3 7,318 x 1.12, below the CFO's mid-teens sequential (+15% = 8,416 [22]) because ~$300M of the Fab 28 loss is 10nm server [21] and the substrate shortage is industry-wide [22]. 2027: Q1 8,100 (second ~$300M Fab 28 hit [21]), then +$350M a quarter as substrate and Intel 3 capacity arrive later in 2027 [18] -> FY2027 34,500 (+28.6% on FY2026 26,832). Demand cross-check: TrendForce server CPU units +40% in 2027 with Arm to ~30% share [17] -> x86 units about +40% x 0.70/0.78 = +26%; AMD keeps gaining (35.5% server unit share Q3 [19]; AMD Data Center +97% y/y [20]), so Intel's unit growth trails x86 and price/mix fills the gap. 2028 9,250-9,550 a quarter (+9%): no 2028 market forecast found; Arm share gains continue [17].
drivers.why: Disclosed segment kept as a driver because it is capacity-bound: demand (TrendForce [17]) exceeds what Intel can ship, so the informative quantity is Intel's own output.
drivers.variant_view: CFO's mid-teens Q4 and +15% a quarter supply adds: FY2027 ~37B, target about +$4; substrate shortage lasting through 2027: FY2027 ~31B, about -$5.

drivers.label: CCPG segment operating margin
drivers.derivation: Actual CCPG operating margin 2025 30.9/26.1/31.6/27.0%, 2026 32.6/26.4/28.2% [1-4]. Q4 2026 22%: revenue down ~20% q/q on a largely fixed cost base (operating deleverage; Q4 company GAAP gross margin guide 37.1% vs 43.0% in Q3 [1]). 2027 23-25% and 2028 25%: volume stays ~10% below 2025, so margin stays below the 2025-26 range (26-33%).
drivers.why: Client margin moves with utilisation of Intel 7/18A client wafers and pricing.

drivers.label: DCAI segment operating margin
drivers.derivation: Actual DCAI margin 2025 13.9/16.1/23.4/26.4%, 2026 30.5/39.5/41.5% [1-4] on server price increases and full utilisation. Q4 2026 36%: Fab 28 wafer write-offs mostly 10nm server [21] and ~200bp company gross-margin hit [18]. 2027 37-39% (shortage pricing persists, Diamond Rapids ramp costs). 2028 34-36%: pricing normalises as capacity adds and Arm/AMD gain share [17,20].
drivers.why: Server pricing and mix are the swing in Intel's profit pool.

drivers.label: Foundry + All Other + corporate + eliminations operating income
drivers.derivation: Actual (total operating income - CCPG - DCAI) 2025 -3,237/-5,862/-2,975/-2,879; 2026 -7,194 (incl. Q1 corporate -5,080 restructuring), -3,021, -2,802 [1-4]. drivers.variant_view: Foundry breakeven path (-1,800 a quarter by 2028): target about +$5; 14A start-up costs without customers (-3,200 a quarter): about -$5.

model_inputs.structure_note: Quarterly driver set (Q1 FY2025-Q4 FY2028; 7 actual quarters). Value carried by (1) P/E on the build's own NTM EPS at the horizon (GAAP EBIT, SBC costed, own interest, interest income and NCI lines), weight 0.65, and (2) a two-part sum of the parts (Products EV/EBIT 15x; Foundry/other/corporate loss x 6), weight 0.35, because Products and Foundry differ in cycle and risk. No FCF-yield leg: forward levered FCF is negative in FY2026-FY2028 (CFO: negative FCF in 2027 [22]). No DCF (policy). The Products SOTP metric (20,700 = FY2028 CCPG + DCAI EBIT from the build) is not driver-linked (the engine's ntm terms cannot read segment revenue); the Foundry part is linked to other_ebit.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (a) exit k = 0.8 on a trough-earnings own P/E (42.9x); k = 0.6 gives 33.6x and about -$4.5 (~-8%); (b) the 14A option adjustment (30% x $60B, ~+$3.3/share); (c) 2028 PC units +3% with no published 2028 forecast; (d) 2024 CCG comparatives used for 2025 rpu actuals were not re-opened (fetch budget exhausted); (e) post-print consensus EPS could not be retrieved (Twelve Data estimates need a higher plan; Zacks/Nasdaq pages unavailable; StockAnalysis/Yahoo snapshots are pre-print), so consensus fields are null. Probable equity financing: below 20% (cash and short-term investments $54.0B [F80,F81] cover the FY2027 FCF gap in the build), so none in the set.
